rules: All semantic authoring changes begin in the data layer. Runtime/process graph changes are derived consequences, never an independent authoring path.
A current data-layer validation PASS is required before process decomposition or graph synthesis.
Any canonical upstream change invalidates previously materialized process/source projections until they are regenerated and lineage is rematerialized.
Any direct downstream source/graph edit invalidates projection lineage even if bidirectional IDs still appear mapped.
Projection lineage records exact upstream and downstream hashes and is verified mechanically after source materialization.

Reusable pattern selection inputs, Data-Layer module expansion, execution projection, and Editor architecture are derived intermediates. Any change to their canonical inputs invalidates them until deterministic rematerialization.

Pattern execution projection is derived only after the full canonical Data Layer and final information-model validation PASS; selected patterns are then mechanically checked for exact graph realization after source materialization.
